title: AIZEN – CreditConnect-EV
summary: AIZEN reports that CreditConnect-EV financed more than 20,000 electric two-wheelers in Indonesia. Borrower income and net emissions effects are not measured.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: AIZEN reports that CreditConnect-EV financed more than 20,000 electric two-wheelers in Indonesia. Borrower income and net emissions effects are not measured. Live lending deployment in Indonesia. The chapter reports the stated benefit but does not independently verify it.
purpose: Use vehicle telemetry and risk scoring to expand electric-vehicle financing.

ratings.reason: The source reports financing more than 20,000 electric two-wheelers, representing improved access to an asset and financing. It does not establish higher borrower income or durable financial security.
The operating financing system supports lending for a previously difficult asset class at reported scale. Portfolio profitability and default improvement are not established.
Lower transport pollution is intended; the chapter does not measure net emissions attributable to the financing program.

ai_role.statement: The chapter describes this system as supporting the stated purpose. Its causal contribution to the benefit has not been separately assessed.

evidence.citation: Contributed use case in International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact, 2025. Information current as of June 2025. The reported outcomes are attributed to the submitting project, not an independent outcome evaluation by ITU.
evidence.title: Use Case 3: AIZEN – CreditConnect-EV

produced_by: Causal conditions are not established separately in the extracted chapter.

headline: CreditConnect-EV expands electric-motorcycle financing

revisions.change: Added the sourced case with separate benefit depth, beneficiary, evidence confidence, and outcome status assessments.

claim_basis: The makers' report is on file. There is no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
